# dlagv2

> Computes the Generalized Schur factorization of a real 2-by-2 matrix pencil (A,B) where B is upper triangular.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlagv2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlagv2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlagv2(
    order,
    A, LDA,
    B, LDB,
    alphar, strideALPHAR,
    alphai, strideALPHAI,
    beta, strideBETA,
    csl,
    snl,
    csr,
    snr
) → Float64Array
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `2 × 2` |  | input/output 2-by-2 matrix A (column-major) |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `A` |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `2 × 2` |  | input/output 2-by-2 upper triangular matrix B (column-major) |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `B` |
| `alphar` | `Float64Array` | out | `2` |  | output array for real parts of eigenvalue numerators |
| ↳ `strideALPHAR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `alphar` |
| `alphai` | `Float64Array` | out | `2` |  | output array for imaginary parts of eigenvalue numerators |
| ↳ `strideALPHAI` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `alphai` |
| `beta` | `Float64Array` | out | `2` |  | output array for eigenvalue denominators |
| ↳ `strideBETA` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `beta` |
| `csl` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the cosine of the left rotation matrix |
| `snl` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the sine of the left rotation matrix |
| `csr` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the cosine of the right rotation matrix |
| `snr` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the sine of the right rotation matrix |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `A`: On entry, the 2 x 2 matrix A. On exit, A is overwritten by the \`\`A-part'' of the generalized Schur form.
- `B`: On entry, the upper triangular 2 x 2 matrix B. On exit, B is overwritten by the \`\`B-part'' of the generalized Schur form.
- `beta`: (`ALPHAR(k)`+i\*`ALPHAI(k)`)/`BETA(k)` are the eigenvalues of the pencil (A,B), $k=1$,2, $i = \sqrt{-1}$. Note that `BETA(k)` may be zero.
- `csl`: The cosine of the left rotation matrix.
- `snl`: The sine of the left rotation matrix.
- `csr`: The cosine of the right rotation matrix.
- `snr`: The sine of the right rotation matrix.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `beta`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlagv2.ndarray(
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    alphar, strideALPHAR, offsetALPHAR,
    alphai, strideALPHAI, offsetALPHAI,
    beta, strideBETA, offsetBETA,
    csl,
    snl,
    csr,
    snr
) → Float64Array
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `2 × 2` |  | input/output 2-by-2 matrix A |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `A` |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `2 × 2` |  | input/output 2-by-2 upper triangular matrix B |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `B` |
| `alphar` | `Float64Array` | out | `2` |  | output array for real parts of eigenvalue numerators |
| ↳ `strideALPHAR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `alphar` |
| ↳ `offsetALPHAR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `alphar` |
| `alphai` | `Float64Array` | out | `2` |  | output array for imaginary parts of eigenvalue numerators |
| ↳ `strideALPHAI` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `alphai` |
| ↳ `offsetALPHAI` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `alphai` |
| `beta` | `Float64Array` | out | `2` |  | output array for eigenvalue denominators |
| ↳ `strideBETA` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `beta` |
| ↳ `offsetBETA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `beta` |
| `csl` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the cosine of the left rotation matrix |
| `snl` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the sine of the left rotation matrix |
| `csr` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the cosine of the right rotation matrix |
| `snr` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the sine of the right rotation matrix |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `A`: On entry, the 2 x 2 matrix A. On exit, A is overwritten by the \`\`A-part'' of the generalized Schur form.
- `B`: On entry, the upper triangular 2 x 2 matrix B. On exit, B is overwritten by the \`\`B-part'' of the generalized Schur form.
- `beta`: (`ALPHAR(k)`+i\*`ALPHAI(k)`)/`BETA(k)` are the eigenvalues of the pencil (A,B), $k=1$,2, $i = \sqrt{-1}$. Note that `BETA(k)` may be zero.
- `csl`: The cosine of the left rotation matrix.
- `snl`: The sine of the left rotation matrix.
- `csr`: The cosine of the right rotation matrix.
- `snr`: The sine of the right rotation matrix.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `beta`

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlagv2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlagv2';

// Define a 2x2 matrix A (column-major):
const csl = new Float64Array( 1 );
const snl = new Float64Array( 1 );
const csr = new Float64Array( 1 );
const snr = new Float64Array( 1 );

const A = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 2.0, 1.0, 3.0 ] );

// Define a 2x2 upper triangular matrix B (column-major):
const B = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0 ] );

// Output arrays:
const alphar = new Float64Array( 2 );
const alphai = new Float64Array( 2 );
const beta = new Float64Array( 2 );

// Compute the Generalized Schur factorization:
dlagv2.ndarray( A, 1, 2, 0, B, 1, 2, 0, alphar, 1, 0, alphai, 1, 0, beta, 1, 0, csl, snl, csr, snr ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'CSL:', csl[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'SNL:', snl[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'CSR:', csr[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'SNR:', snr[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLAGV2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLAGV2 computes the Generalized Schur factorization of a real 2-by-2 matrix pencil (A,B) where B is upper triangular. This routine computes orthogonal (rotation) matrices given by `CSL`, `SNL` and `CSR`, `SNR` such that

1) if the pencil (A,B) has two real eigenvalues (include 0/0 or 1/0

types), then

$$
\begin{bmatrix} a_{11} & a_{12} \\ 0 & a_{22} \end{bmatrix} := \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CSL} & \mathrm{SNL} \\ -\mathrm{SNL} & \mathrm{CSL} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} a_{11} & a_{12} \\ a_{21} & a_{22} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CSR} & -\mathrm{SNR} \\ \mathrm{SNR} & \mathrm{CSR} \end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
\begin{bmatrix} b_{11} & b_{12} \\ 0 & b_{22} \end{bmatrix} := \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CSL} & \mathrm{SNL} \\ -\mathrm{SNL} & \mathrm{CSL} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} b_{11} & b_{12} \\ 0 & b_{22} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CSR} & -\mathrm{SNR} \\ \mathrm{SNR} & \mathrm{CSR} \end{bmatrix}
$$

2) if the pencil (A,B) has a pair of complex conjugate eigenvalues,

then

$$
\begin{bmatrix} a_{11} & a_{12} \\ a_{21} & a_{22} \end{bmatrix} := \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CSL} & \mathrm{SNL} \\ -\mathrm{SNL} & \mathrm{CSL} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} a_{11} & a_{12} \\ a_{21} & a_{22} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CSR} & -\mathrm{SNR} \\ \mathrm{SNR} & \mathrm{CSR} \end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
\begin{bmatrix} b_{11} & 0 \\ 0 & b_{22} \end{bmatrix} := \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CSL} & \mathrm{SNL} \\ -\mathrm{SNL} & \mathrm{CSL} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} b_{11} & b_{12} \\ 0 & b_{22} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CSR} & -\mathrm{SNR} \\ \mathrm{SNR} & \mathrm{CSR} \end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
\quad\text{where}\quad b_{11} \ge b_{22} > 0
$$

</section>
